about: Runtime platform status from the latest retained installed-package evidence for each platform. Release 0.3.0 supersedes the 0.2.0 macOS limitation; entries without newer installed evidence retain their earlier evidence and limits. A cross-build or newer source test is not release qualification. scripts/catalogue.py reads this file, checks every evidence path exists, and publishes it in the layer catalogue. This catalogue does not qualify 0.4.0.

statuses.supported: The released runtime installs and uninstalls, its background service starts and becomes ready, and an application's default resolution reaches it. Listed limits bound the platforms and behaviors with recorded qualification.
statuses.supported without background services: The programs install, run in the foreground and uninstall. No background service is registered, and default resolution finds no runtime.
statuses.unsupported: The released package has no qualified protected runtime service on this platform. Its default resolution and protected calls remain unavailable.

platforms.name: Windows x64, per-user installation
platforms.runtime: Per-user MSI; the supervisor starts the runtime in the signed-in session.
limits: The 0.3.0 installed job used Windows x64. ARM64 is cross-built; installation on ARM64 hardware is untested.

evidence.shows: Successful 0.3.0 verify job on head ff281d02: private non-admin per-user install and cross-tool compatibility; predecessor upgrade and reinstall; non-default-folder upgrade; failed-upgrade rollback and same-version host restart; uninstall and test-session removal.

platforms.name: Windows x64, machine installation
platforms.runtime: Machine MSI; a service template starts a per-session runtime for each signed-in user.
limits: Everyone installation requires elevation. Runtime instances run in each signed-in user session.
The 0.3.0 installed job used Windows x64. ARM64 is cross-built; installation on ARM64 hardware is untested.

evidence.shows: Successful 0.3.0 verify job on head ff281d02: machine-scope forced-failure rollback, upgrade exclusion and predecessor removal; fresh interactive session and crash recovery; uninstall for everyone and test-session cleanup.

platforms.name: Linux amd64 with a systemd user manager
platforms.runtime: Per-user tarball; install.sh registers abstraction-runtime.service with the user manager.
limits: Trusted selection needs clone3 and waitid P_PIDFD (Linux 5.4 or newer); a sandbox denying them returns PROOF_UNAVAILABLE.

0.3.0 package qualification passed 26 installed Linux cases, with lifecycle evidence from WSL2 and a hosted Ubuntu amd64 runner. ARM64 installation, other distributions and graphical sessions are untested.

evidence.shows: Successful 0.3.0 linux-verify job: checksum, install, package inspection and uninstall, plus the Linux disposable-account installed-lifecycle job.

0.2.0 candidate on hosted Ubuntu: installation under a disposable account and systemd user manager, readiness, a real download, result observation, removal with retained data and process cleanup passed.

platforms.name: Linux amd64 without a systemd user manager (containers, WSL without systemd, hosted CI accounts)
platforms.runtime: The same tarball; install.sh installs the programs, reports that no background service will run and records `timer no`.
limits: Default resolution cannot select a runtime: selection reads the loaded user unit from systemctl, so applications receive runtime_unavailable.
0.3.0 package qualification includes the no-user-manager installation check. `openabstractions serve runtime` runs in the foreground; an application reaches it only through an explicit endpoint.

evidence.shows: Successful 0.3.0 linux-verify job includes install, package inspection and uninstall; the run's Linux package qualification includes the no-user-manager installation check.

0.2.0 release: installation without a user manager, the openabstractions payload, absence of retired jobd/dl/jobctl executables and removal passed. This job does not establish foreground capability calls.

platforms.name: macOS (universal package; installed qualification on arm64)
platforms.runtime: The signed and notarized 0.3.0 universal package installs for the current user. Installed XPC discovery, capability readiness and protected-call behavior passed on the available arm64 Mac; reinstall and removal passed.
limits: The universal package includes Intel binaries, but installed execution was tested only on arm64 hardware.
The retained installed receipt covers install, XPC discovery/calls, reinstall and removal; it does not record a separate crash-injection recovery test.
Path names compare byte for byte on macOS although its volumes ignore case by default, so two names OA keeps apart can name one file (abstraction-identity CONTRACT.md, SamePathName).
Native providers are not available on macOS in 0.4.0: their caller check needs an XPC endpoint. The macOS package leaves out Local model stores (inventoryd) and the model host (modelhostd).

evidence.shows: The 0.3.0 universal package is signed, notarized and published. Its installed acceptance was run on an arm64 Mac; Intel hardware execution was not tested.

Exact package SHA-256 82a2ec559ae47cf6f5fe8460fdb98c227867bac19ae855e3e2db4f4851b7b7fa; package verification, install, XPC readiness and protected-call checks, reinstall and removal passed on macOS 26.6.2 arm64.

platforms.name: Android, including Termux
platforms.runtime: None. No runtime is built, packaged, installed or run for Android.
limits: The packager builds only linux and macos; the release builds Windows MSIs, Linux tarballs and one macOS package.
Termux has no systemd user manager, which Linux selection requires.

evidence.shows: The release builds no Android asset.
Nothing in the tree records a build, install or run on Android or Termux.
